claim.text: Research-period backtest: Sharpe 1.8, annual return 7%, maximum drawdown 8%.

exhibits.summary: Delaying the signal by 1 more bar moves the Sharpe ratio from 1.81 to 1.77 (change -0.04).
Under strict point-in-time data the Sharpe ratio moves from 1.81 to 1.81. Strict mode changed no field or operator the signal uses.
At 10 bps the Sharpe ratio is 1.76 (as submitted, 5 bps: 1.81); it breaks even at above 200 bps with daily turnover 0.01.
On the full universe the Sharpe ratio is 0.27 against 1.81 as submitted; the strategy never saw 107 delisted assets.
On the sealed period (strict mode, 10 bps) the Sharpe ratio is 0.40 against 1.81 in research, a gap of +1.41.
The best year gives 21% of total P&L (year 8) and calm regimes give 149%; Sharpe is 3.84 in calm and -3.23 in stressed regimes.
The log holds 3 distinct specs; the best of 3 under no edge is expected to reach a Sharpe of 0.22, so the claimed 1.80 becomes 1.58 and the probability that the true Sharpe is above zero is 100%.
The real signal's gross Sharpe of 1.85 beats 100% of 200 shuffled signals (shuffled mean -0.02, 95th percentile 0.56).
Perturbing the 2 numeric values in the signal by up to 50% moves the Sharpe ratio from 1.81 to as low as 1.13 (as low as 1.32 at 25%).
The top 1% of days (20 days) give 26% of total P&L and the top 5 assets give 25% (net of the strategy's own costs).

series.label: cumulative share of P&L, best days first

verdict.opinion: Rejected: core test damaging (survivorship_test EX-4, holdout_test EX-5).
